NEXB Tablet App

Overview

NEXB is the tablet app BNK Busan Bank staff use at the counter. A banker sits next to a customer, opens the customer’s assets as a report, and talks through them on one shared screen.

Money is a serious subject, so the app uses a friendly character and soft shapes to keep the conversation relaxed.

Who uses it

Branch staff, with the customer sitting alongside and looking at the same screen.

How it is used

A customer’s assets are analysed and shown as a dashboard and a report that both people read together.

What it replaces

Rigid internal screens that felt like reading a spreadsheet.

Design intent

Designed a shared consultation experience that makes complex financial information easier for bank staff and customers to navigate and discuss.

UX approach

Two design decisions shaped much of the app. Each starts from a problem in a real consultation and states what the design is meant to make easier.

Floating Tabs

Problem

Bank staff move between several task screens during a consultation.

Design decision

Floating Tabs keep up to eight work screens open and let staff switch between them from a fixed bar at the bottom of the display.

Intended benefit

Staff keep the context of the work in progress while they handle several consultation tasks.

  • Keeps up to eight work screens open at once.
  • Stays fixed at the bottom of every screen.
  • Collapses and expands, so the screen stays focused on the task.
  • Closes tabs one by one or all at once.
  • Keeps the state of each screen when staff switch away from it.

Shared consultation experience

Problem

The complex internal work screens are hard to explain while sitting with a customer.

Design decision

The customer’s financial information is visualized as dashboards and analysis reports.

Intended benefit

Staff and customer look at the same screen, understand the information and talk it through together.

Principles behind both

Show assets as a story

Analysis results come first as charts and short summaries. Tables follow for detail.

Design for two readers

The customer watches the same screen, so the tone stays soft even though the topic is money.

Give the character a job

It greets, explains, reassures and fills empty moments, and it stays clear of the data.

Key screens

The main flow of a consultation, from signing in to showing the customer their report.

Sign in and home

Customer management

Analysis reports

The customer report is the center of the app. It gathers deposits, funds, trusts and loans in one view and compares the customer’s asset mix with peers of the same age and investment profile.

Recommendations, loan balance changes, rate benefits and fee waivers follow as short cards, so the banker can walk the customer through them in order.

Typography

Pretendard is the base typeface. It replaces the mobile app’s Spoqa Han Sans because a tablet needs larger sizes, more weights and wider platform support.

StyleSize / lineWeights
Display 148 / 62Black, Medium
Display 232 / 48Black, Medium
Title28 / 42Black, Medium
Body 120 / 30Bold, Medium, Regular
Body 218 / 27Bold, Medium, Regular
Caption 116 / 24Bold, Medium, Regular
Caption 214 / 21Bold, Medium, Regular

Letter spacing is −0.5 px for Display 1 and −0.2 px for everything else.

Grid and layout

Designed for Galaxy Tab S9 (2560 × 1600) and S10+ (2800 × 1752). Both are 16:10, so the working canvas is 1200 × 750.

Customer status
Content area
1200 × 750 canvas
GNB 56 Top bar 32

Sizes are set in rem so the whole layout scales in proportion. Image assets are exported at 3×.

Spacing

An 8 pt grid, with 4 pt and 2 pt steps for tight details. Space shows how closely things are related.

Within an item

2 / 4 / 8. Icon and text, label and field, title and body in a card.

Within a group

16 / 24. List items and cards in the same section.

Between sections

32 / 40. Section breaks and screen margins. Dense areas get 32 or more.

Elevation

Five layers ordered by what the user should notice first. Surfaces and lines do most of the work, and color plus shadow mark what can be acted on.

  • 0 BaseBackground, disabled items
  • 1 PassiveLists, tables, text fields
  • 2 ActivePrimary buttons, selection controls, key cards
  • 3 FixedSide navigation (GNB)
  • 4 OverlayModals and pop-ups over a dimmed screen

Navigation

Navigation keeps the consultation in view. The customer’s status is always the first thing in the top bar.

Top bar

Shows whether trading and consultation are available, then the customer’s name. Quick buttons cover menu search, calculator, alerts and calendar, and the staff member’s own menu sits at the right. It stays fixed while the page scrolls.

Side navigation and drawer

The side bar stays on every screen and the current area is shown in red. A drawer slides out from the left for detailed tasks.

Floating tabs

Up to eight open screens stay at the bottom of the display, so a banker can switch tasks without losing work in progress. Tabs close one by one or all at once.

Three levels of tabs

Underlined tabs for the main level, pill tabs for the second level, and segmented tabs for quick switching between two to five options.

Data visualization

Each chart answers one kind of question. The goal is that a customer can read it without help.

  • Compare. Bar and radar charts for sizes and balance between items.
  • Composition. Donut and stacked charts for shares of a whole.
  • Trend. Line charts for change over time, and gauges for progress to a goal.

Charts from the customer report: asset mix against peers, a monthly transaction pattern, loan balance change, rate benefits and fee waivers.

Feedback and status

Loading

A layer over the current screen for short waits, and a full-screen state when a screen change takes longer.

Empty states

A small icon and one line inside a card or list. On a whole page, the character explains what happened and offers a next step.

Success and error

Success messages are short and do not interrupt the work. Errors and warnings share one pattern, so staff never have to guess the difference.

Brand identity

NEXB stands for the next generation of digital banking. The logo turns the initial N into a symbol of expansion and forward motion.

Infinite Expansion & Forward Momentum

The logo makes the first letter, N, into the symbol. It brings innovation, connection, evolution and growth into one form, with the endless growth of the banking experience as its core idea.

Symbol: a layered N

A solid N sits over translucent layers. The layers add depth, and the flowing shape borrows from the infinity sign.

Logotype: a forward arrow

An arrow sits in the middle of the E. It points toward the future and toward where each consultation is heading.

Five meanings of “Next”

  • Next BankingA next-generation digital banking experience.
  • Next BridgeA bridge that connects new generations.
  • Next BusinessDigital transformation of corporate banking and sales consultation.
  • Next BeyondA branch experience that goes past its limits.
  • Next BranchAn intelligent platform that grows through AI and data-led consultation.

Character

The character is the emotional touchpoint of NEXB. Its job is to explain the situation, show empathy and soften the moment, and the data does the informing.

Its pink body takes its outline from the B in the logo, and every pose wears a BNK staff badge.

  • Keep it off screens that are dense with information.
  • Never place it over a main call to action. Use the empty centre or the margins.
  • Let the character carry the feeling first, then the text.

Twelve poses cover the moments of a consultation: greeting, searching, typing, handling a card, celebrating, and worry.

In the app

From 2D to 3D motion

The flat line character was extended into a 3D version and brought to life with AI-generated motion for promotion.

The same face appears in the app, as in the attendance challenge, and in campaign motion, so staff meet one consistent character wherever the brand shows up.
